arxiv-1802-05565.title: Quantum interactions, Predictability and Emergence Of Gravity
arxiv-1802-05565.creator: Vyshnav Mohan
arxiv-1802-05565.description: Abstract In this paper, we will show that gravity can emerge from an effective field theory, obtained by tracing out the fermionic system from an interacting quantum field theory, when we impose the condition that the field equations must be Cauchy predictable.

arxiv-2104-02364.title: FIMP Dark Matter from Leptogenesis in Fast Expanding Universe
arxiv-2104-02364.creator: Zhi-Fang Chang, Zhao-Xuan Chen, Jia-Shu Xu, Zhi-Long Han
arxiv-2104-02364.description: Abstract Within the framework of canonical type-I seesaw, a feebly interacting massive particle (FIMP) χ \chi is introduced as a dark matter candidate. The leptogenesis mechanism and dark matter relic density share a common origin via decays of Majorana neutrinos N N .

arxiv-2106-15238.title: Representation based meta-learning for few-shot spoken intent recognition
arxiv-2106-15238.description: Abstract Spoken intent detection has become a popular approach to interface with various smart devices with ease. However, such systems are limited to the preset list of intents-terms or commands , which restricts the quick customization of personal devices to new intents. This paper presents a few-shot spoken intent classification approach with task-agnostic representations via meta-learning paradigm.

Due to the complexity of the high-dimensional text, these reviews are often simplified as a single numerical score, e.g., ratings or sentiment scores. arxiv-2301-00996.title: Transactional Composition of Nonblocking Data Structures
arxiv-2301-00996.creator: Wentao Cai, Haosen Wen, Michael L. Scott
arxiv-2301-00996.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Wentao Cai, Haosen Wen, Michael L. Scott. This paper introduces nonblocking transaction composition (NBTC), a new methodology for atomic composition of nonblocking operations on concurrent data structures. Unlike previous software transactional memory (STM) approaches, NBTC leverages the linearizability of existing nonblocking structures, reducing the number of memory accesses that must be executed together, atomically, to only one per operation in most cases (these are typically the linearizing instructions of the constituent operations).

arxiv-2310-03098.title: NOCAP: Near-Optimal Correlation-Aware Partitioning Joins CCS: Information systems Join algorithms CCS: Theory of computation Database query processing and optimization (theory)
arxiv-2310-03098.creator: Zichen Zhu, Xiao Hu, Manos Athanassoulis
arxiv-2310-03098.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zichen Zhu, Xiao Hu, Manos Athanassoulis. Storage-based joins are still commonly used today because the memory budget does not always scale with the data size. One of the many join algorithms developed that has been widely deployed and proven to be efficient is the Hybrid Hash Join (HHJ), which is designed to exploit any available memory to maximize the data that is joined directly in memory. However, HHJ cannot fully exploit detailed knowledge of the join attribute correlation distribution.

arxiv-2311-00533.title: The Eclipse Layout Kernel
arxiv-2311-00533.creator: Sören Domrös, Reinhard von Hanxleden, Miro Spönemann, Ulf Rüegg, Christoph Daniel Schulze
arxiv-2311-00533.description: Abstract The elk ( elk ) is a collection of graph drawing algorithms that supports compound graph layout and ports as explicit anchor points of edges. It is available as open-source library under an EPL license. Since its beginning, elk has served both as a research vehicle for graph drawing algorithms, and as a practical tool for solving real-world problems.

arxiv-2407-15667.title: On even K K -groups over p p -adic Lie extensions of global function fields
arxiv-2407-15667.creator: Meng Fai Lim
arxiv-2407-15667.description: Abstract Let p p be a fixed prime number, and let F F be a global function field with characteristic not equal to p p . In this paper, we shall study the variation properties of the Sylow p p -subgroups of the even K K -groups in a p p -adic Lie extension of F F .

arxiv-2409-01062.title: Defending against Model Inversion Attacks via Random Erasing
arxiv-2409-01062.creator: Viet-Hung Tran, Ngoc-Bao Nguyen, Son T. Mai, Hans Vandierendonck, Ngai-man Cheung
arxiv-2409-01062.description: Abstract Model Inversion (MI) is a type of privacy violation that focuses on reconstructing private training data through abusive exploitation of machine learning models. To defend against MI attacks, state-of-the-art (SOTA) MI defense methods rely on regularizations that conflict with the training loss, creating explicit tension between privacy protection and model utility.

arxiv-2507-21940.title: The interplay of μ \mu -dichotomy, bounded growth, and spectral properties via growth rate comparisons. Thanks: ∗ This author was partially supported by ANID, Beca de Doctorado Nacional 21220105.
arxiv-2507-21940.creator: Néstor Jara ∗, Claudio A. Gallegos
arxiv-2507-21940.description: Abstract . We investigate the behavior of the dichotomy spectrum of nonautonomous linear systems under general growth rates. By introducing comparison criteria we clarify how μ \mu -dichotomy and μ \mu -bounded growth interact. We also study the evolution of the dichotomy spectrum under these comparisons, revealing that faster growth rates compress the spectrum, while slower growth rates expand it.

arxiv-2510-08026.title: PEAR: Phase Entropy Aware Reward for Efficient Reasoning
arxiv-2510-08026.creator: Chen Huang, Wenxuan Zhang
arxiv-2510-08026.description: Abstract Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have achieved impressive performance on complex reasoning tasks by generating detailed chain-of-thought (CoT) explanations. However, these responses are often excessively long, containing redundant reasoning steps that inflate inference cost and reduce usability. Controlling the length of generated reasoning without sacrificing accuracy remains an open challenge.

arxiv-2510-19617.title: Propius: A Platform for Collaborative Machine Learning across the Edge and the Cloud
arxiv-2510-19617.creator: Eric Ding, Cornell University
arxiv-2510-19617.description: Abstract Collaborative Machine Learning is a paradigm in the field of distributed machine learning, designed to address the challenges of data privacy, communication overhead, and model heterogeneity. There have been significant advancements in optimization and communication algorithm design and ML hardware that enables fair, efficient and secure collaborative ML training. However, less emphasis is put on collaborative ML infrastructure development.

pmc-11603307.creator: Bin Fang, Juan Lai, Yongfeng Liu, Lin-lin Liu, Xiao Yu, Xiang Li, Haili Ke, Xianfeng Zhang, Xin Zhang
pmc-11603307.description: Human adenoviruses (HAdVs) are highly contagious and have significant clinical implications in the pediatric population. The phylogenetic analyses based on the whole genome and genes revealed distinct sub-clusters within HAdV-B and -E.

pmc-12549707.title: Locally advanced primary urethral carcinoma in an HIV-positive female patient: report of a case successfully managed with definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy at a referral cancer center in Abidjan
pmc-12549707.creator: Evrard Narcisse Séka, Corneille Téa Saki, Amara Gozana Tuo, Paul Hyacinthe Foua Bi
pmc-12549707.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Female Primary urethral carcinoma is a rare malignancy frequently diagnosed at an advanced stage. Surgery, the most common treatment modality, is associated with substantial functional impairment. Here, we present the case of a 45-year-old HIV-positive woman with locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma infiltrating the bladder, vagina, and left obturator muscle, treated with definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy combining fractionated external beam radiotherapy and weekly cisplatin. The treatment resulted in complete remission, which was sustained after 25 months of follow-up.

pmc-12574394.description: IntroductionDespite the known haemostatic action of emicizumab (Hemlibra) in haemophilia A patients, its role in the prevention and control of bleeding in high-demand haemostatic situations, such as major surgery, remains to be determined. Patients receiving regular emicizumab prophylaxis often require concomitant factor VIII (FVIII) therapy during major surgery to prevent uncontrolled bleeding and to promote postoperative healing.

pmc-12606264.title: Trapped between darkness and heat: desert birds (Argya squamiceps) initiate daily activity earlier (and terminate it later) in response to heat
pmc-12606264.creator: Yitzchak Ben Mocha, Itamar Ring, Oded Keynan
pmc-12606264.description: Diurnal desert endotherms must adjust the timing of their daily activity to mitigate physiological stress from ambient heat. Understanding the limits of this behavioural plasticity is important for predicting how climate change may affect desert species. Here, we studied the onset and termination of daily activity in wild birds (Arabian babblers Argya squamiceps) inhabiting the Arava Desert.

pmc-12692922.title: The Effect of Graphene Oxide Deposited on Titanium Surface on Structural, Corrosion, and Biological Properties
pmc-12692922.creator: Kamila Narojczyk, Barbara Nasiłowska, Agata Lange, Marta Kutwin, Sławomir Jaworski, Łukasz Krzowski, Wiktoria Kasprzycka, Piotr Olejnik, Maciej Chrunik, Aneta Bombalska, Zdzisław Bogdanowicz
pmc-12692922.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The article presents the results of structural, corrosion, microbiological, biological, and genotoxicity studies on the effect of graphene oxide deposited on a flat titanium foil surface, intended for use, in general, implantology and other medical applications. The methodology of graphene oxide (GO) deposition involved a surface cleaning process combined with RF plasma activation, followed by the application of a thin layer of dispersed aqueous GO suspension using a spin coater.

pmc-12963916.title: Efficacy and safety of cardioneuroablation as a treatment for patients with functional bradyarrhythmia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12963916.creator: Aiyue Chen, Tao Zhang, Huanling Sun, Bin Tu, Pakezhati Maimaitijiang, Xinyi Wang, Lihui Zheng
pmc-12963916.description: Cardioneuroablation (CNA) is a novel procedure that shows promising results in patients with functional bradyarrhythmia, including functional sinus node dysfunction (SND) and atrioventricular block (AVB). We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of CNA in this population. PubMed, Embase and Web of Science were searched from January 2005 to August 2025 following PRISMA guidelines.
